date.source: The arena report's own dateline: "VENUE & DATE: Tokyo Korkuen Hall - 11/15/98"; posted 19 November 1998 and reposted 25 November 1998.

matches.note: Miyazaki won by referee stoppage at 5:47 after a series of strikes left Ruas unable to continue.
Billed as "Doug Thomas" here, on loan from a rival promotion, he won by cross armbreaker at 4:10 in a rematch of an earlier real-world draw between the two.
Dean, also on loan from a rival promotion, won by released dragon suplex at 2:03 amid rumours of a contract dispute over his own booking.
Sunjinski won by pinfall at 4:53 with his own Firesquad jackhammer suplex.
Mayashi won by rolling armbar at 9:37 after Karloff briefly turned a guillotine choke aside with an illegal elbow strike.
Shirow won by Fujiwara armbar at 5:27.
The main event, billed as the rubber match of a rivalry already two wins apiece with a riot-ending draw; Fukada was disqualified for a low blow after Asamiya had him in a choke hold.

evidence.source: the promotion's own arena report on its debut card, posted twice under slightly different headlines
evidence.note: Seven matches before a reported 2,200-fan sellout, broadcast live on Japanese network television.

date.source: The arena report's own dateline: "VENUE & DATE: Tokyo Dome - 11/28/98"; posted in three parts on 7 December 1998.

matches.note: World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final. Asamiya won by Fujiwara armbar submission at 10:58 after targeting Sunjinski's shoulder, injured earlier in a bar fight.

World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final, billed as "Ed Dean" v. Eiji Miyazaki. Declared a double disqualification at 8:20 after a brawl spilled to the floor; the tournament committee ruled the bracket slot forfeit and advanced Asamiya to the final on a bye rather than holding a second semi-final.
World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final, billed as Takashi Fukada v. "Doug Thomas." Fukada won by rolling kneebar submission at 6:44.

World Heavyweight Championship tournament quarter-final. Shirow won by STF submission at 4:11 of a five-minute overtime period, after regulation time expired with Mayashi apparently tapped out; the finish stood for a total match time of 19:11.
A special bonus bout added to replace the tournament's own cancelled second quarter-final, outside the bracket. Karloff won by heel hook submission at 5:45.
The promotion's first Super-Middleweight exhibition, a non-title bout under a ten-minute time limit with no overtime; ruled a time-limit draw.

World Heavyweight Championship tournament semi-final (Asamiya having already advanced to the final on the bye above). Fukada won by front face-lock choke submission at 10:07, reversing a Shirow arm-bar attempt.

World Heavyweight Championship tournament final, crowning the promotion's first champion. Fukada won at 1:43 of overtime when the referee stopped the bout after ruling Asamiya's arm injury (aggravated from his own quarter-final) prevented him from continuing.

evidence.source: the promotion's own arena report on its second event, posted in three parts
evidence.note: Eight fights before a reported crowd of 58,000 at the Tokyo Dome, broadcast live on Japanese network television; an eight-fighter single-elimination tournament (not the sixteen an earlier reading of a founding announcement had projected) crowned the promotion's first World Heavyweight Champion.
